subsection.p: The little segments are not solution curves. They are instructions for solution curves. A true solution curve must pass through the field by matching the local direction at each point.

note.title: Direction field
note.p: a direction field or slope field is a plot of small line segments, where the segment at (t,y) has slope F(t,y).

subsection.p: The direction field is especially helpful when the equation is hard to solve exactly. It can show whether solutions rise or fall, whether they approach a stable value, and how different initial conditions change the behavior.

exercise.title: What is a direction field a picture of?

statement.p: The equation y'=F(t,y) assigns a slope to each point (t,y). In your own words, why are the little segments not themselves solution curves, and what instruction do they give to any true solution that passes through a point?

hint.p: Each segment is a local direction, not a whole history. A solution curve must match the prescribed slope at every point it visits.

paragraphs.title: Warning: a direction field is not a uniqueness proof
paragraphs.p: A direction field can suggest that one solution curve passes through each point. For many equations in this chapter, that is true. But it is not automatic.
For t<0, both sides are 0. At t=0, the derivative is also 0. So this piecewise function solves the same initial value problem.
Two different solution curves pass through the same initial point.

warning.title: What the warning teaches
warning.p: A direction field is a powerful picture, but it is still a picture. Clean uniqueness requires hypotheses on the function F(t,y). In this chapter, our examples will be well behaved, but we should remember that the warning exists.

paragraphs.p: The direction field gives the geometry of a differential equation. The next question is computational. If the field tells us the slope at every point, can we follow those slopes one small step at a time and build an approximate solution curve?
That step-by-step method is Euler’s method.

exercise.title: Why is a direction field not a uniqueness proof?

statement.p: A field may look as if one curve passes through each point, yet y'=\sqrt{|y|} with y(0)=0 has more than one solution. In your own words, what does the picture fail to guarantee, and why does the physical domain of a model matter even when the mathematics continues?

hint.p: Clean uniqueness needs hypotheses on F(t,y). A model of population, for example, should not be interpreted for negative values even if the equation still has behavior there.
